newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Palau sign preliminary aviation pact.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Palau sign preliminary aviation pact.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday signed an official aviation agreement with the Micronesian resort island of Palau despite the absence of diplomatic ties, Taiwan's Civil Aeronautics Administration said.
In the initial agreement signed by Taiwan and Palau officials at a hotel in the Philippines, the sides agreed to provide full flight service effective immediately, the ministry said in a statement.
Under the agreement signed by Taiwan's aviation director Tsai Duai and a Palau trade minister, airlines from the sides would be allowed to operate four weekly flights.
Palau President Kuniwa Nakamura was on hand to witness the signing of the preliminary pact.
The sides will work on the details by June 16 and sign a final agreement on July 31, the statement said.

Palau has no diplomatic relations with Taiwan or arch rival China but has warm business ties with Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party, which pledged in 1995 to invest US$8 million to build a six-storey hotel in Palau.
